::: {.callout-important}
San Francisco is a prominent center of Autonomous Vehicle (AV) activity. Data describing AV activity in San Francisco, however, is spread across multiple sources, redacted from public reports, collected with insufficient detail, or in some cases not collected at all. Please see [Transparency](./transparency.html) for more information.

This section primarily reports statewide values due to the limitations noted above. 
:::

This section presents data from the California Department of Motor Vehicles (California DMV) and California Public Utilities Commission (CPUC).  

## Vehicle Miles Traveled

```{python}
#| label: fig-vmt-company-permit
#| fig-cap: "VMT by Company and Permit Type"
#| cap-location: margin

fig4 = px.line(
    vmt_long.loc[:,['date','label','vmt']], 
    x='date', 
    y='vmt',
    color='label',
    color_discrete_map=company_permit_type_color_map,
    line_dash='label',
    line_dash_map=company_permit_type_dash_map,
    #height=500,
)

fig4.update_layout(
    legend=dict(
        title='',
        orientation='h'
        ),
    yaxis_title=None,
    xaxis_title=None,
)
fig4.show()
```

::: {.column-margin}
Vehicle miles traveled (VMT) grew gradually from 2020 through 2023 when Waymo's VMT began to expand more rapidly.  Waymo has reported more VMT than other companies in each permit category for most of its history.  

::: {.callout-important}
It is not possible to sum VMT across all permit types to get total VMT because VMT reported to DMV may overlap with VMT reported to CPUC, and because VMT has historically been reported to DMV only under testing permits, but not under deployment permits.  
:::

:::

```{python}
#| label: fig-vmt-phase
#| fig-cap: "VMT by Phase"

fig5 = px.area(
    period_vmt.loc[:,['company','date','period','period_vmt']], 
    x='date', 
    y='period_vmt',
    facet_col='company',
    color='period',
    color_discrete_map=period_color_map,
)
fig5.for_each_annotation(lambda a: a.update(text=a.text.split("=")[-1]))

fig5.update_layout(
    legend=dict(
        title='',
        orientation='h'
        ),
    yaxis_title=None,
    xaxis_title=None,
)
fig5.show()
```

::: {.column-margin}
The CPUC categorizes passenger service into 3 periods: 

- Period 1. A vehicle is empty and waiting for a passenger to request a ride
- Period 2. Driving to pick up a passenger
- Period 3. Transporting the passenger.  

Data by period of service is reported to CPUC by companies operating under deployment permits.  Waymo is the only company currently operating driverless deployment passenger service.  Their VMT throughout California has grown consistently over time with only a few notable dips.  Cruise briefly operated driverless deployment passenger service before their permit was suspended and eventually revoked.  
:::

```{python}
#| label: fig-pmt-vmt
#| fig-cap: "Passenger Mileage Efficiency"

synth_da = trip_long[['date']].drop_duplicates()
synth_da['label'] = 'Drive alone'
synth_da['pmt_over_vmt'] = 1
synth_bus = synth_da.copy()
synth_da['label'] = 'Bus'
synth_da['pmt_over_vmt'] = 12.6

fig7 = px.line(
    pd.concat(
        [trip_long.loc[:,['date','label','pmt_over_vmt']],
         synth_da,
         synth_bus
        ]
    ), 
    x='date', 
    y='pmt_over_vmt',
    color='label',
    color_discrete_map=company_permit_type_color_map,
    line_dash='label',
    line_dash_map=company_permit_type_dash_map,
)

fig7.update_layout(
    legend=dict(
        title='',
        orientation='h'
        ),
    yaxis_title=None,
    xaxis_title=None,
    ).update_traces(
    visible="legendonly", 
    selector=lambda t: t.name in ["Bus"]
)

fig7.show()
```

::: {.column-margin}
Weighted vehicle occupancy measures how many miles people travel for each vehicle mile, calculated as person miles traveled (PMT) / VMT.  Driving alone, long considered the least-efficient mode has a weighted vehicle occupancy of 1.  AVs have a weighted vehicle occupancy less than 1 because they drive empty in between passenger trips.  Weighted vehicle occupancy for a bus in San Francisco was 12.6 in 2024.  
:::


```{python}
#| label: fig-deadheading
#| fig-cap: "Deadheading"

fig8 = px.line(
    trip_long.loc[:,['date','label','deadhead_rate']], 
    x='date', 
    y='deadhead_rate',
    color='label',
    color_discrete_map=company_permit_type_color_map,
    line_dash='label',
    line_dash_map=company_permit_type_dash_map,
)

fig8.update_layout(
    legend=dict(
        title='',
        orientation='h',
        ),
    yaxis=dict(
        range=(0,1)
    ),
    yaxis_title=None,
    xaxis_title=None,
)
fig8.show()
```

::: {.column-margin}
AV passenger services drive around empty in between trips in period 1 and period 2 described above.  This is called deadheading.  Deadheading decreased over time before leveling-off slightly over 40% of all miles driven in passenger service.  
:::

## Passenger Trips

```{python}
#| label: fig-trips-company-permit
#| fig-cap: "Passenger Trips by Company and Permit Type"

fig1 = px.line(
    trip_long.loc[:,['date','label','trips']], 
    x='date', 
    y='trips',
    color='label',
    color_discrete_map=company_permit_type_color_map,
    line_dash='label',
    line_dash_map=company_permit_type_dash_map,
)
fig1.update_layout(
    legend=dict(
        title='',
        orientation='h'
        ),
    yaxis_title=None,
    xaxis_title=None,
    )
fig1.show()
```

::: {.column-margin}
Passenger trips are reported for companies operating under CPUC pilot and deployment permits.  Under pilot permits, a single statewide number is reported by month.  Under deployment permits, trips are reported by Census Tract.  
:::


```{python}
#| label: fig-trips-company-county
#| cap-location: margin
#| fig-cap: "Passenger Trips by Company and County"

fig3 = px.bar(
    trip_county_long.loc[:,['date','label','trips_start']], 
    x='date', 
    y='trips_start',
    color='label',
    color_discrete_map=company_county_color_map,
).update_traces(
    dict(marker_pattern_fgcolor=unknown_hash_color,
         marker_pattern_shape='/',
         opacity=0.75
        ),
    selector=({'legendgroup':'Waymo Unidentified'}),
)

fig3.update_layout(
    legend=dict(
        title='',
        orientation='h'
        ),
    yaxis_title=None,
    xaxis_title=None,
    )

fig3.show()
``` 

::: {.column-margin}

In December 2024, the last month Waymo reported unredacted tract-level trip data, about 74% of trips were in San Francisco, 25% in Los Angeles, and less than 1% in San Mateo.  Since then, it is not clear where growth is happening or whether Waymo has expanded into new markets.

::: {.callout-important}
Waymo began redacting tract-level trip data in the first quarter of 2025. The county-level totals below are derived from tract-level data and therefore only statewide totals are shown from 2025 on.

Waymo is currently the only company with approval to provide paid passenger service in California.
:::

:::

::: {.callout-important}
Waymo reported tract-level data using 2010 Census Tract definitions, while Cruise used 2020 Census Tract definitions.  To preserve accuracy, and because Waymo reported orders of magnitude more trips than Cruise, Cruise trips were re-apportioned from 2020 Census Tracts to 2010 Census Tracts in this map.
:::
